advisories.title: Leafnode connections can corrupt shared user permissions
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports leafnode connections and subject permissions for configured users.

### Problem Description

Leafnode connection handling could modify shared user permissions, allowing subject restrictions to be bypassed. Concurrent access to those permissions could also cause server crashes, memory disclosure or memory corruption. The reporter demonstrated code execution on local test builds. The issue affects leafnode listeners that authenticate against configured users with subject permissions.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * Report reference: GHSA-p849-62j6-rhc5
 * Credit: Claude; Anthropic security team in collaboration with Anthropic Research

advisories.title: Client-supplied identity fields can bypass authorization callouts
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

Authorization callout service users can be exempted from callouts so the service can connect without recursively invoking itself.

### Problem Description

The exemption decision could use client-supplied identity fields that did not correspond to the credentials actually authenticated. A connection could be treated as an exempt service user and skip the external authorization decision. This bypass did not require possession of the exempt identity’s credentials, although other local authentication requirements could still apply.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-vqv6-8g5v-c9c4>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Memory-backed stream purges can cause excessive CPU use
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

JetStream permits authorized users to purge messages from a stream, including by subject and sequence.

### Problem Description

For memory-backed streams, some purge operations could perform work according to a supplied sequence bound rather than the messages actually present. An authorized purge request could hold the stream’s storage lock and consume excessive CPU, blocking operations on that stream and degrading server availability.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-rr37-7hx9-8xw5>
 * Credit: @kalash33

advisories.title: Leafnode peers can forge JetStream acknowledgements outside their permissions
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

JetStream uses acknowledgement messages to track processing and, for some retention policies, determine when stored messages can be removed.

### Problem Description

The leafnode ingress path accepted JetStream acknowledgement subjects without evaluating the leafnode user’s publish permissions. A peer with restricted leafnode access could affect consumer state in its account and cause messages to be removed or cease redelivery without acknowledgement from the intended consumer.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-r9gv-x84w-62mr>
 * Credit: @manus-pi

advisories.title: Certificate-mapped identities can authenticate by password on another listener
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server can map TLS client certificates to configured users. Multiple listeners can share user definitions while using different authentication settings.

### Problem Description

A certificate-only identity with an empty password could be accepted using username and empty-password authentication on another listener where certificate mapping was not enabled. Knowledge of the configured identity could therefore be sufficient to connect without the intended client certificate. Leafnode, WebSocket and MQTT listeners could provide the alternate path.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-q57r-qh7g-9wgm>
 * Credit: @larrasket

advisories.title: JetStream restore format detection can buffer excessive data
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

JetStream accepts stream backups from authorized users and detects the backup format before restoring a stream.

### Problem Description

The format-detection stage could retain incoming compressed data without a finite buffer limit while waiting for recognizable output. A user allowed to restore streams could cause excessive memory use and disrupt the server process. Account stream-storage limits did not bound this temporary detection buffer.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-p8x9-xrv7-3g8j>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Authorization callouts did not enforce JWT source restrictions
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

Authorization callouts can return user JWTs that restrict the source networks from which a user is allowed to connect.

### Problem Description

The server accepted callout-issued user credentials without enforcing their source-network restrictions. A valid credential could be used from an otherwise disallowed source if the server listener was reachable. The returned subject permissions still applied, but the intended network restriction did not.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-p29q-ccgc-hcg7>
 * Credit: Thai Son Dinh, VinSOC Labs (R&D) (@sondt99)

advisories.title: Removing TLS certificate pins does not revoke existing client connections
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports certificate pinning and can recheck active client connections when TLS pin settings change during configuration reload.

### Problem Description

The reload check used the previous pin set instead of the newly loaded one. A client using a removed pin could remain connected even though the operator intended to revoke its access. NATS, MQTT and WebSocket client checks were affected.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-mf72-w5mg-h2mg>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: MQTT internal subscriptions can bypass topic deny rules
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS MQTT support uses internal subjects to store and deliver messages. User-facing subscribe permissions apply to the original topic namespace.

### Problem Description

MQTT clients could subscribe directly to internal message subjects that were not covered by the original topic deny rules. A client denied access to a topic could consequently receive message contents through an internal alias in the same account. The fix described here covers MQTT-protocol subscriptions; native NATS-client access is a separate related issue.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-m996-6cph-cjhc>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Malformed MQTT and counter records can terminate the server
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server decodes stored MQTT state and JetStream responses, and can maintain counters sourced from other streams.

### Problem Description

Several decoding paths did not safely handle missing or null fields. Malformed MQTT state, internal responses or sourced counter records could trigger an unrecovered panic and terminate the server process. Some malformed MQTT records could remain in storage and cause a further failure when read after restart. Exposure depends on access to the affected internal subjects or source configuration.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-hwrp-2926-g93m>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Unexpected MQTT acknowledgements can consume JetStream storage
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server maintains persistent state for MQTT QoS 2 delivery using JetStream.

### Problem Description

The server could store delivery state in response to MQTT acknowledgements that did not correspond to an outstanding QoS 2 delivery. A connected client could cause unnecessary persistent records to accumulate and exhaust storage available to its account, disrupting MQTT service for other users of that account.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.15.1. No fixed v2.14.x release was identified through v2.14.10. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-hm5m-vqj5-vf2q>
 * Credit: @SounLabs

advisories.title: Malformed JWT permission subjects can terminate the server
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

In operator mode, account administrators issue signed user credentials containing subject permissions.

### Problem Description

A signed user credential containing a malformed permission subject could pass claim validation and later trigger a panic while the server installed its permissions. An administrator of a trusted account could cause denial of service beyond that account. Equivalent malformed permissions in configuration files were rejected.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-h9r4-8j36-3c2f>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Leafnode permissions can be bypassed for internal MQTT subjects
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server uses internal account subjects for MQTT messages and session management. Leafnode connections can be assigned subject-level permissions.

### Problem Description

Broad internal MQTT subject exceptions also applied to leafnode connections. A restricted leafnode peer could bypass its allow list for MQTT traffic and control messages in its account. Depending on the available MQTT state, this could disclose message contents or allow interference with sessions and retained messages.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-gc58-jp35-x246>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Pre-CONNECT no_auth_user handling can bypass authorization callouts
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports no_auth_user for clients that connect without explicit credentials and can delegate authentication decisions to an authorization callout.

### Problem Description

The pre-CONNECT protocol path could register the configured no_auth_user without consulting the authorization callout. A connection rejected by the normal authentication flow could therefore be admitted with that user’s permissions. The issue affects deployments that combine these features.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Remove no_auth_user from the server configuration and, if configured, from the websocket block. Clients must then use the normal authentication handshake. Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-g9p6-654w-mr9v>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Leafnode peers can bypass publish permissions for JetStream acknowledgements
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

Leafnode user permissions restrict which subjects a remote leafnode may publish to the hub. JetStream acknowledgements update consumer delivery state.

### Problem Description

Inbound leafnode permission checks exempted JetStream acknowledgement subjects. A leafnode peer could submit acknowledgements outside its configured publish permissions and cause pending work to be acknowledged or terminated. For streams whose retention depends on acknowledgements, this could remove messages without processing by the intended consumer.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-fwrx-9r9q-h7p4>
 * Credit: @Hama1cco

advisories.title: MQTT packet buffering can cause memory and CPU exhaustion
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server receives and assembles MQTT packets before processing their contents.

### Problem Description

Post-CONNECT packet assembly could buffer data beyond the configured payload-derived limit and repeatedly copy the accumulated data. A client sending an oversized or slowly completed packet could consume excessive memory and CPU before message-level checks ran. This could deny service to other clients and accounts, including users of other protocols.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-c5hj-fqj4-pj32>
 * Credit: Thai Son Dinh, VinSOC Labs (R&D) (@sondt99)

advisories.title: Queue-scoped deny permissions were inconsistently enforced
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS subscription permissions can deny access to a subject for a particular queue group, including when broader wildcard subscriptions are permitted.

### Problem Description

Queue-qualified deny rules were interpreted inconsistently across subscription admission, message delivery and permission refresh. A broader subscription could receive messages covered by a queue-specific deny, and some existing subscriptions were not revoked as expected. Related parsing inconsistencies also affected publish denies and leafnode import restrictions.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Replace queue-qualified deny entries with subject-only deny entries in the permission configuration, including leafnode deny_imports where applicable. This also denies access to the subject outside the specified queue group, so it is suitable only where that broader restriction is acceptable. Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-9qgw-9q78-p7xv>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: MQTT listener OCSP peer verification can be silently omitted
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server allows TLS and OCSP peer verification to be configured separately for the MQTT listener.

### Problem Description

MQTT OCSP setup consulted the top-level TLS settings instead of the listener-specific settings. A deployment that enabled OCSP peer verification specifically for MQTT could therefore accept client certificates without the configured revocation check. Normal certificate-chain validation does not substitute for this missing revocation check.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-8xmc-886f-g496>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Oversized MQTT subscription packets can exhaust server resources
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server parses MQTT subscription requests before registering the requested subscriptions.

### Problem Description

The MQTT packet reader did not consistently apply a configured finite size bound after CONNECT. Oversized subscription packets could reach buffering and filter parsing despite max_payload, causing excessive allocations. Subscription-count limits applied later and did not prevent these parsing costs. Resource exhaustion could affect the entire server process.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-8fcg-2fq8-c8qc>
 * Credit: @X1AOxiang

advisories.title: Ordinary users in an authorization account can receive callout requests
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS authorization callouts send authentication requests to a designated account. These requests can contain credentials and other sensitive connection information.

### Problem Description

Ordinary users placed in the authorization account were not consistently prevented from subscribing to callout requests. Additional gaps affected programmatically omitted account settings and permission refresh after account updates. A user sharing that account could receive authentication information intended only for the authorization service.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-7mrx-vpq7-fhmp>
 * Credit: @inanna-malick

advisories.title: Connected MQTT clients can bypass packet buffering limits
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports MQTT clients over TCP and WebSocket and uses payload limits to constrain incoming data.

### Problem Description

After MQTT connection establishment, packet buffering did not consistently enforce the configured payload-derived size limit. A client could cause excessive buffering and copying before later processing checks were applied. This could exhaust memory or CPU and affect all accounts and protocols served by the process. Authentication is required only where the MQTT listener is configured to require it.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-72gq-694q-fj66>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Authorization callouts did not enforce allowed connection types
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

Authorization callouts return signed user credentials that can restrict the connection types a user is permitted to use.

### Problem Description

The callout authentication path did not enforce the effective user credential’s allowed connection types before accepting a connection. A credential intended for one transport or connection role could be used on another listener governed by the same callout. This could permit a leafnode connection where only ordinary client access was intended.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-724w-jvcm-4c58>
 * Credit: @SounLabs

advisories.title: OCSP responses were not bound to the certificate being checked
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports OCSP checks to determine whether a TLS certificate has been revoked.

### Problem Description

OCSP validation verified the response signature without consistently checking that the response described the certificate being evaluated. A valid response for another certificate from the same issuer could therefore be accepted. Under the required conditions, a revoked certificate could pass the affected revocation check.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-65q4-982r-rm5c>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Invalid snapshot delivery subjects can leak server resources
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

JetStream allows authorized users to request a stream snapshot and specify the subject used to deliver it.

### Problem Description

Snapshot requests accepted delivery subjects that the snapshot notification mechanism could not use. Such requests could leave background work and associated resources unreleased. Repeated requests could exhaust process resources; some streams could also remain unable to produce further snapshots until the server restarted.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-5xw9-67vx-qppr>
 * Credit: Taeyoung Jeong (@ttzero25)

advisories.title: Remote queue subscription weights can exhaust server memory
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server uses queue subscription weights to distribute messages across cluster routes and leafnodes.

### Problem Description

An accepted route or leafnode peer could supply a queue weight that caused the server to allocate excessive memory while resolving matching subscriptions. Message delivery could stall, and memory exhaustion could terminate the process. A cluster listener without authentication increases exposure to this issue.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-5v9x-4f9q-q7qj>
 * Credit: @X1AOxiang

advisories.title: Route and cluster URL credentials can be exposed by debug endpoints
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server provides optional monitoring and profiling endpoints. Some debug responses include the server command-line arguments.

### Problem Description

Redaction of command-line credentials did not cover route and cluster URL arguments. When those arguments contained credentials, monitoring or profiling responses could disclose them to anyone able to access the relevant endpoints. The issue requires credentials in command-line URLs and an accessible monitoring or profiling listener.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.11.17, v2.12.8, v2.14.0 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Move route and cluster URLs containing credentials from command-line arguments into the server configuration file. Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-5qvj-hvwx-q9qf>
 * Credit: Koda Reef (@kodareef5)

advisories.title: Route pool index panic
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server cluster peers exchange connection metadata when establishing routes. Routes can operate with or without connection pooling.

### Problem Description

Route pool metadata was not fully validated when a peer did not use pooling. A peer accepted on the cluster listener could cause an out-of-range access and terminate the server process. Cluster authentication limits who can reach the affected path; a compromised authorized peer can still trigger it.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-4fpp-8grw-j976>
 * Credit: @smaeljaish771

advisories.title: HTTPS leafnode proxies can receive credentials without TLS
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server can establish outgoing leafnode connections through an HTTP CONNECT proxy.

### Problem Description

An HTTPS proxy URL was accepted without establishing TLS to the proxy before sending the CONNECT request. Proxy credentials could consequently be exposed to an observer on the network path to the proxy. TLS between the leafnode and its destination does not protect this separate proxy exchange.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-42wr-c22f-4h5c>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Scoped signing key templates can bypass required proxy authentication
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server supports scoped signing keys and authorization callouts that assign user permissions and connection restrictions. A user can be required to connect through an authenticated proxy.

### Problem Description

The server did not consistently enforce the proxy requirement after applying a scoped signing key template. A user whose effective template required a proxy could establish a direct connection without the expected proxy authentication. Both direct JWT authentication and authorization callouts were affected.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.8 and v2.15.1. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-2wxw-wgx7-4ffx>
 * Credit: ARSB (@ARSB1)

advisories.title: Remote queue subscription weights can exhaust server memory
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server exchanges subscription interest with cluster routes and leafnodes, including information about queue subscribers.

### Problem Description

A route or leafnode peer could advertise a queue subscription weight that caused excessive memory allocation when matching messages. The work occurred while holding a subscription-list lock and could stall message delivery or terminate the server through memory exhaustion. An attacker requires access to a route or leafnode connection accepted by the server.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.9 and v2.15.2. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-27c4-m7hq-v6pw>
 * Credit: thc1006 (蔡秀吉)

advisories.title: NATS Server: Remote crash via integer overflow in Connz pagination
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, a client able to send account-scoped connection monitoring requests could crash the server by supplying Connz pagination Offset and Limit values that overflowed internal arithmetic before the response window was safely bounded. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: NATS Server: MQTT-over-WebSocket Path Can Crash WebSocket-Only JetStream Servers Before MQTT Is Enabled
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, a WebSocket listener could route requests for the MQTT-over-WebSocket path into MQTT handling even when MQTT was not configured, allowing an unauthenticated client with access to the WebSocket listener to reach uninitialized MQTT state and crash the server process. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: NATS Server: MQTT retained and QoS replay bypass subscribe deny filters
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, MQTT retained message delivery and QoS1+ durable replay could deliver messages whose original topics matched a subscriber configured subscribe deny rule because these delivery paths did not consistently recheck the concrete original topic before sending the MQTT PUBLISH to the subscriber. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: NATS Server: MQTT partial CONNECT packets can exhaust pre-auth memory
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, an unauthenticated MQTT client could cause the server to retain large incomplete MQTT CONNECT packets before authentication completed, consuming server memory while the parser waited for the advertised MQTT packet length. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: NATS Server: `no_auth_user` pre-CONNECT fast path bypasses user connection restrictions
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, a client could be registered as the configured no_auth_user through a parser path used when the first client operation was not CONNECT, bypassing user-level connection restrictions such as allowed_connection_types or proxy_required that normal authentication would apply. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: Pre-auth panic and server hang via malformed JWT issuer (missing Ed25519 length check in nkeys)
advisories.summary:
### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server can run in operator mode, deriving client identities and permissions from JWT credentials signed with NKEYs.

### Problem Description

An unauthenticated client could cause an operator-mode NATS Server to panic while processing a client JWT before authentication completed.

The issue involved accepting a truncated public account key, which could later reach Ed25519 signature verification with an invalid length. The malformed key was taken from JWT claims processed during authentication before a client identity had been established.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.1, v2.12.9 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.2 and v2.12.10.

### Workarounds

No known workaround for operator-mode deployments using JWT authentication. Upgrade to a fixed release.

Deployments not using operator-mode JWT authentication are not affected by this issue.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-g33f-6538-grxh>
 * Credit: @queencitycyber

advisories.title: NATS Server: MQTT SUBSCRIBE Protocol Injection via Leaf Node/Route Forwarding allows arbitrary NATS command injection
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.1 and 2.12.9, an MQTT client could include protocol control characters in subscription filters that were later forwarded as NATS protocol data to route or leafnode connections, corrupting the forwarded protocol stream and allowing injection of unintended NATS protocol operations. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.1 and 2.12.9.

advisories.title: NATS Server: MQTT subscribe ACL bypass via $MQTT.deliver.pubrel prefix (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33217)
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.12, an authenticated MQTT client could subscribe to the internal $MQTT.deliver.pubrel subject family, bypassing configured subscribe permissions and exposing MQTT QoS2 protocol metadata for sessions in the account. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.12.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33249: Leaf node connections bypass Nats-Trace-Dest permission check
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.3 and 2.12.8, message trace destination checks were applied to ordinary client connections but not consistently to messages arriving through leafnode connections, allowing a leafnode operator to send trace events to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and to use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.3 and 2.12.8.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Pre-auth server crash via double INFO in leafnode handshake
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.12.8 and 2.11.17, an unauthenticated peer with network access to a leafnode listener with compression enabled could crash the server during the pre-authentication leafnode handshake by sending repeated leafnode INFO protocol messages before authentication and account setup completed. This issue is fixed in versions 2.12.8 and 2.11.17.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Queue Subscribe Authz Bypass
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16, an authenticated user with subscription deny permissions could bypass a plain subject deny rule by using a queue subscription, because queue-specific deny evaluation could override the plain subject deny result when the queue name itself was not denied. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Subscribe Authz Bypass via Wildcard-Overlap
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16, an authenticated user could receive messages on denied subjects when a wildcard subscription overlapped with a configured wildcard deny rule but was not a subset of it, and queue subscriptions could also affect delivery to legitimate queue consumers. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Route API Auth Bypass
advisories.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16, when no_auth_user was configured, a parser fast path intended for ordinary client connections could also apply to route or leafnode listeners, allowing an unauthenticated peer to bypass inter-server CONNECT authentication and operate with the privileges associated with that connection type. This issue is fixed in versions 2.14.0, 2.12.7, and 2.11.16.

advisories.title: NATS: Pre-auth remote server crash via WebSocket frame length overflow in wsRead
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Starting in version 2.2.0 and prior to versions 2.11.14 and 2.12.5, a missing sanity check on a WebSockets frame could trigger a server panic in the nats-server.  This happens before authentication, and so is exposed to anyone who can connect to the websockets port. Versions 2.11.14 and 2.12.5 contains a fix. A workaround is available. The vulnerability only affects deployments which use WebSockets and which expose the network port to untrusted end-points. If one is able to do so, a defense in depth of restricting either of these will mitigate the attack.

advisories.title: NATS Server panic via malicious compression on leafnode port
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.14 and 2.12.5, if the nats-server has the "leafnode" configuration enabled (not default), then anyone who can connect can crash the nats-server by triggering a panic. This happens pre-authentication and requires that compression be enabled (which it is, by default, when leafnodes are used). Versions 2.11.14 and 2.12.5 contain a fix. As a workaround, disable compression on the leafnode port.

advisories.title: NATS has MQTT plaintext password disclosure
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, for MQTT deployments using usercodes/passwords: MQTT passwords are incorrectly classified as a non-authenticating identity statement (JWT) and exposed via monitoring endpoints. Versions 2.11.14 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, ensure monitoring end-points are adequately secured. Best practice remains to not expose the monitoring endpoint to the Internet or other untrusted network users.

advisories.title: NATS is vulnerable to MQTT hijacking via Client ID
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. The nats-server provides an MQTT client interface. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.5, Sessions and Messages can by hijacked via MQTT Client ID malfeasance. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.5 patch the issue. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: NATS allows MQTT clients to bypass ACL checks
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, when using ACLs on message subjects, these ACLs were not applied in the `$MQTT.>` namespace, allowing MQTT clients to bypass ACL checks for MQTT subjects. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: NATS: Leafnode connections allow spoofing of Nats-Request-Info identity headers
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. The nats-server offers a `Nats-Request-Info:` message header, providing information about a request. This is supposed to provide enough information to allow for account/user identification, such that NATS clients could make their own decisions on how to trust a message, provided that they trust the nats-server as a broker. A leafnode connecting to a nats-server is not fully trusted unless the system account is bridged too. Thus identity claims should not have propagated unchecked. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, NATS clients relying upon the Nats-Request-Info: header could be spoofed. This does not directly affect the nats-server itself, but the CVSS Confidentiality and Integrity scores are based upon what a hypothetical client might choose to do with this NATS header. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: NATS Server: Incomplete Stripping of Nats-Request-Info Header Allows Identity Spoofing
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, the NATS message header `Nats-Request-Info:` is supposed to be a guarantee of identity by the NATS server, but the stripping of this header from inbound messages was not fully effective. An attacker with valid credentials for any regular client interface could thus spoof their identity to services which rely upon this header. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: NATS has pre-auth server panic via leafnode handling
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, a client which can connect to the leafnode port can crash the nats-server with a certain malformed message pre-authentication. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, disable leafnode support if not needed or restrict network connections to the leafnode port, if plausible without compromising the service offered.

advisories.title: NATS is vulnerable to pre-auth DoS through WebSockets client service
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, a malicious client which can connect to the WebSockets port can cause unbounded memory use in the nats-server before authentication; this requires sending a corresponding amount of data. This is a milder variant of CVE-2026-27571. That earlier issue was a compression bomb, this vulnerability is not. Attacks against this new issue thus require significant client bandwidth. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, disable websockets if not required for project deployment.

advisories.title: NATS JetStream has an authorization bypass through its Management API
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, users with JetStream admin API access to restore one stream could restore to other stream names, impacting data which should have been protected against them. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, if developers have configured users to have limited JetStream restore permissions, temporarily remove those permissions.

advisories.title: NATS has mTLS verify_and_map authentication bypass via incorrect Subject DN matching
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, when using mTLS for client identity, with `verify_and_map` to derive a NATS identity from the client certificate's Subject DN, certain patterns of RDN would not be correctly enforced, allowing for authentication bypass. This does require a valid certificate from a CA already trusted for client certificates, and `DN` naming patterns which the NATS maintainers consider highly unlikely. So this is an unlikely attack. Nonetheless, administrators who have been very sophisticated in their `DN` construction patterns might conceivably be impacted. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, developers should review their CA issuing practices.

advisories.title: NATS credentials are exposed in monitoring port via command-line argv
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, if a nats-server is run with static credentials for all clients provided via argv (the command-line), then those credentials are visible to any user who can see the monitoring port, if that too is enabled. The `/debug/vars` end-point contains an unredacted copy of argv. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. As a workaround, configure credentials inside a configuration file instead of via argv, and do not enable the monitoring port if using secrets in argv. Best practice remains to not expose the monitoring port to the Internet, or to untrusted network sources.

advisories.title: NATS: Message tracing can be redirected to arbitrary subject
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. Starting in version 2.11.0 and prior to versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6, a valid client which uses message tracing headers can indicate that the trace messages can be sent to an arbitrary valid subject, including those to which the client does not have publish permission. The payload is a valid trace message and not chosen by the attacker. Versions 2.11.15 and 2.12.6 contain a fix. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: nats-server websockets are vulnerable to pre-auth memory DoS
advisories.summary: NATS-Server is a High-Performance server for NATS.io, a cloud and edge native messaging system. The WebSockets handling of NATS messages handles compressed messages via the WebSockets negotiated compression. Prior to versions 2.11.2 and 2.12.3, the implementation bound the memory size of a NATS message but did not independently bound the memory consumption of the memory stream when constructing a NATS message which might then fail validation for size reasons. An attacker can use a compression bomb to cause excessive memory consumption, often resulting in the operating system terminating the server process. The use of compression is negotiated before authentication, so this does not require valid NATS credentials to exploit. The fix, present in versions 2.11.2 and 2.12.3, was to bounds the decompression to fail once the message was too large, instead of continuing on. The vulnerability only affects deployments which use WebSockets and which expose the network port to untrusted end-points.
